intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Join locals for picnics beneath thousands of blooming sakura trees, enjoy street food stalls selling yakitori and dango, and soak in the festive atmosphere. Perfect for families with open spaces for children to play.

experiences.name: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a breathtaking world of interactive digital art installations where light, sound, and color blend seamlessly. Children and adults alike will be mesmerized by the borderless rooms that react to movement. A truly unique cultural and artistic experience that blends technology with Japanese aesthetics.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Japan's most iconic food market with a guided family-friendly walking tour. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette), matcha sweets, and grilled seafood skewers. Learn about Japanese culinary traditions and the importance of fresh ingredients in Japanese cuisine. Kids will love the variety of street snacks.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo forest of Arashiyama, then hike up to the Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Families can feed the monkeys from inside a viewing hut while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a rickshaw ride through the scenic area for extra fun.

experiences.name: Traditional Samurai and Ninja Experience
experiences.description: Dress your family in authentic samurai armor or ninja costumes and learn basic sword techniques and ninja skills from trained instructors. This hands-on cultural workshop gives children and adults a thrilling glimpse into Japan's feudal history. Includes a photo session in full costume and a certificate of completion for the kids.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

Perfect for families with open spaces for children to play.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport around 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect baggage, and take the airport limousine bus or train to your accommodation (Aegean Bliss Resort). Convenience store run at FamilyMart or 7-Eleven for late-night snacks and essentials.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Convenience store bento box or onigiri from 7-Eleven or Lawson near the hotel (budget-friendly, ~¥500–¥800)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase an IC card (Suica or ICOCA) at the airport for seamless transit throughout your trip. Exchange some yen at the airport kiosk. Rest well — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a late breakfast, explore the area around your hotel. If near a beach or coastal area, take a relaxing morning stroll along the shoreline and enjoy the spring sea breeze.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local market or shopping street (shotengai) to pick up snacks, souvenirs, and get a feel for everyday Japanese life. Look for 100-yen shops (Daiso or Seria) for budget supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local izakaya (Japanese pub) for your first proper Japanese dinner. Order yakitori skewers, edamame, and draft beer or soft drinks. Great for families — many izakayas are family-friendly.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a convenience store pastry and canned coffee (~¥400)
meals.lunch: Ramen shop near the hotel — a hearty bowl typically costs ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Local izakaya dinner — budget ~¥1,200–¥1,800 per person including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Use this day as a gentle orientation day. Download Google Maps offline for Japan and install a translation app with camera feature (Google Translate). Check local cherry blossom forecast updates.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Kyoto via Shinkansen or JR express train (use your IC card). Head straight to Maruyama Park for the famous Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami). Arrive early to find a good spot under the iconic weeping cherry tree. Bring a picnic mat and snacks from a convenience store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Higashiyama district on foot. Walk through Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka stone-paved lanes lined with traditional shops and tea houses. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple (¥500 entry) for panoramic views of Kyoto framed by cherry blossoms.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the lantern-lit Gion district at dusk — free to walk and beautiful in the evening. Dine at a budget teishoku (set meal) restaurant in Gion for a complete Japanese meal.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store onigiri and green tea before departing (~¥400)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in Maruyama Park — buy bento boxes and snacks from a nearby convenience store or market stall (~¥800)
meals.dinner: Teishoku set meal in Gion area — rice, miso soup, grilled fish, pickles (~¥900–¥1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-April is peak cherry blossom season in Kyoto — Maruyama Park will be stunning. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Kiyomizudera can be crowded; go in the afternoon for slightly thinner crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Start early and head to Arashiyama Bamboo Grove. Walk through the towering bamboo forest — it's free and most magical in the early morning before crowds arrive. Explore the surrounding Tenryuji Temple garden (¥500) with its beautiful spring scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park (¥550 adults, ¥250 children) — a fantastic family activity! See wild Japanese macaques up close and enjoy sweeping views of Kyoto from the hilltop. Kids will love it.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto and visit Nishiki Market — Kyoto's famous covered food market. Sample street food like tamagoyaki (egg rolls), fresh tofu, and pickled vegetables. Great for budget grazing.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before heading out (~¥500)
meals.lunch: Yudofu (tofu hot pot) at a budget restaurant near Arashiyama — a Kyoto specialty (~¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Nishiki Market food stalls and street snacks — budget ~¥800–¥1,200 for a satisfying grazing dinner

day_by_day.notes: The Monkey Park hike is about 15–20 minutes uphill — bring water. Children must be supervised near the monkeys. Arashiyama is best explored on foot or by rented bicycle (¥1,000/day from local shops).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha — the iconic shrine with thousands of vermilion torii gates. Entry is free! Hike as far up the mountain as energy allows. The lower section takes about 30 minutes; the full hike is 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short train ride to Nara (about 45 minutes from Kyoto). Visit Nara Park to see the friendly wild deer (¥200 for deer crackers). Walk to Todaiji Temple (¥600) to see the giant bronze Buddha — awe-inspiring for families.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your hotel base. Relax and enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel. Take an evening walk to enjoy the spring night air.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — keep it light before hiking (~¥400)
meals.lunch: Kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) in Nara — a local specialty available at markets (~¥800–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Gyudon (beef rice bowl) at Yoshinoya or Sukiya near the hotel — budget ~¥500–¥700

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free and open 24/7 — arrive early to avoid crowds. In Nara, the deer are wild — keep food out of sight when not feeding them. Children should be supervised as deer can be pushy!

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Osaka (30 minutes from Kyoto by train). Visit Osaka Castle Park — the castle grounds are free to explore and beautiful with cherry blossoms still in bloom. The castle museum costs ¥600 but the park is worth the visit alone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dotonbori, Osaka's vibrant entertainment district. Walk along the canal, take photos with the giant Glico Running Man sign, and explore the lively streets. Visit the free observation areas and street performers.
day_by_day.evening: Osaka is the food capital of Japan — indulge in takoyaki (octopus balls, ~¥500) and okonomiyaki (savory pancake, ~¥800) at budget street stalls and standing restaurants in Dotonbori.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel (~¥400)
meals.lunch: Kushi-katsu (breaded skewers) at a standing bar in Shinsekai area — ~¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Takoyaki + okonomiyaki street food feast in Dotonbori (~¥1,000–¥1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is extremely family-friendly and lively. The Dotonbori area is safe and walkable. Use your IC card for all train travel between cities — it's the most budget-efficient option.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Osaka's Kuromon Ichiba Market — known as 'Osaka's Kitchen.' Browse fresh seafood, local produce, and street snacks. A great cultural and culinary experience. Entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the train to the Tennoji area. Visit Tennoji Zoo (¥500 adults, ¥200 children) — one of Japan's oldest zoos and a great family activity. Afterward, explore Tennoji Park and the surrounding area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Dotonbori or Namba area for evening shopping at Don Quijote (a massive discount store open late — great for souvenir shopping at low prices). Grab ramen for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tamagoyaki and seafood samples at Kuromon Market (~¥600)
meals.lunch: Bento from Kuromon Market or a nearby soba restaurant (~¥800)
meals.dinner: Ramen at a local shop in Namba — hearty tonkotsu or shoyu ramen (~¥800–¥1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tennoji Zoo is budget-friendly and children love it. Don Quijote is excellent for buying Japanese snacks, beauty products, and quirky souvenirs at competitive prices.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Himeji — take the JR Shinkansen or express train from Osaka (about 30–45 minutes). Visit Himeji Castle, one of Japan's most stunning and best-preserved castles. Entry is ¥1,000 adults, ¥300 children. The castle grounds and cherry blossom trees are spectacular in April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kokoen Garden adjacent to the castle (¥310 combo ticket available) — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with spring flowers in bloom. Walk back through Himeji city center.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Osaka or your hotel base. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and early rest to recharge.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store before departing (~¥500)
meals.lunch: Anago (sea eel) bento box — a Himeji local specialty available at train station shops (~¥1,000–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Udon at a local restaurant near the hotel — light and budget-friendly (~¥700–¥900)

day_by_day.notes: Himeji Castle is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most photogenic spots in Japan. The castle interior has steep staircases — not suitable for very young children or those with mobility issues. Book train tickets in advance during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Return to your hotel's beach area for a relaxing morning. Enjoy the coastal scenery, take a morning swim if weather permits, or simply relax on the beach. Reflect on the trip and let the kids play freely.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local shrine or temple for a peaceful cultural experience. Many smaller shrines are free to enter and offer a quieter alternative to the major tourist sites. Try your hand at writing an ema (wooden wish plaque, ~¥500).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a nice but budget-friendly Japanese restaurant. Try shabu-shabu or sukiyaki at an all-you-can-eat restaurant (nomi-tabehoudai) — many offer lunch and dinner sets for ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a special treat at a local bakery — melon pan or croissants (~¥500)
meals.lunch: Chirashi sushi (scattered sushi bowl) at a local sushi restaurant — ~¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: All-you-can-eat shabu-shabu or sukiyaki farewell dinner (~¥1,500–¥2,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to do any last-minute souvenir shopping. Great budget souvenir options: matcha KitKats, local sembei (rice crackers), tenugui towels, and 100-yen shop items. Pack carefully tonight for your departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Japan! Wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the beach or a nearby park. Visit a local convenience store for your final Japanese breakfast — a perfect sendoff ritual.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and travel to the airport with plenty of time. Use your remaining yen on airport shopping — tax-free stores at Japanese airports offer good deals on cosmetics, snacks, and alcohol.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 10 wonderful days of cherry blossoms, culture, amazing food, and family memories in Japan!

meals.breakfast: Final convenience store breakfast — onigiri, tamagoyaki sandwich, and canned matcha latte (~¥600)
meals.lunch: Airport ramen or sushi restaurant — treat yourself to a proper last meal (~¥1,200–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Return your IC card at the airport for a refund of the remaining balance (minus a ¥220 handling fee). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before your international flight. Keep receipts for any tax-free purchases — you may need to show them at customs.

day_by_day.morning: Rest — flight arrives at 22:30, no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest — flight arrives at 22:30, no afternoon activities scheduled
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange private airport transfer or Narita Express to your hotel. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your room. Light convenience store snack run to a nearby 7-Eleven or FamilyMart for Japanese onigiri, instant ramen, or snacks — a fun first taste of Japan.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) — onigiri, sandwiches, hot foods, and drinks (~¥500–¥1,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance. Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. Exchange some yen at the airport currency counter or use a 7-Bank ATM. Hydrate well after the long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a late breakfast, take a leisurely stroll around the hotel's beachfront area to get your bearings. Explore the local neighborhood, visit a nearby shrine or garden if available, and pick up any essentials from a local pharmacy or convenience store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest city center for a gentle orientation walk. Visit a local shopping street (shotengai) or department store basement food hall (depachika) to browse regional snacks, bento boxes, and fresh produce. Pick up a pocket Wi-Fi or SIM card if not already arranged. Browse a 100-yen shop (Daiso or Seria) for fun family souvenirs and supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at a mid-range family-friendly izakaya (Japanese gastropub) near the hotel. Order a variety of small dishes — yakitori skewers, edamame, karaage fried chicken, miso soup, and rice — to introduce the family to Japanese dining culture. Return to the hotel early for a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet or nearby café — Japanese set breakfast with rice, miso soup, grilled fish, and tamagoyaki (~¥800–¥1,500 per person)
meals.lunch: Depachika bento box or local ramen shop (~¥900–¥1,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Local izakaya — shared small plates, grilled skewers, and soft drinks/beer (~¥2,000–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery day — avoid over-scheduling. Jet lag is real, especially for families with children. Aim for an early bedtime to reset circadian rhythms for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Tokyo for a full day of exploration. Start at the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — join a guided family-friendly walking tour through Japan's most iconic food market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki egg omelets, fresh fruit skewers, and seafood snacks. Kids will love the vibrant atmosphere and trying new foods. The tour typically runs 2–3 hours and is a fantastic cultural immersion experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market tour, walk or take a short taxi to the teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum. Immerse the whole family in breathtaking interactive digital art installations where light, sound, and movement blur boundaries between art and visitor. Allow 2–3 hours to explore all the rooms. Book tickets in advance online as this popular attraction sells out quickly.
day_by_day.evening: Wind down with dinner in the Odaiba or Shibuya area depending on proximity. Visit the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at dusk — one of the world's busiest pedestrian crossings and a quintessential Tokyo experience. Grab dinner at a nearby conveyor-belt sushi restaurant (kaiten-zushi) for a fun, interactive family meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab-and-go from a convenience store before departing (~¥800–¥1,200 per person)
meals.lunch: Included tastings on the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour, supplemented with additional market stall purchases (~¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi conveyor belt sushi restaurant near Shibuya or Odaiba (~¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab Borderless tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance — they frequently sell out, especially on weekends. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the market tour. The Tsukiji Outer Market tour is best experienced on an empty or light stomach to maximize tasting opportunities.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen (bullet train) to Kyoto — a thrilling experience in itself for families. Book reserved seats in advance. Arrive in Kyoto and head directly to Maruyama Park for the Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience. Mid-April is the tail end of cherry blossom season, so expect beautiful late blooms or early green leaves with scattered petals — still magical. Spread a picnic blanket under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree and enjoy the serene atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Gion district — Kyoto's historic geisha quarter. Walk along Hanamikoji Street and Shirakawa Canal lined with traditional machiya townhouses. If lucky, spot a maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to an appointment. Visit Yasaka Shrine adjacent to Maruyama Park, which is free to enter and beautifully atmospheric.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Kyoto kaiseki-inspired set dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Gion. Look for restaurants offering a 'course meal' with seasonal Kyoto vegetables (kyo-yasai), tofu dishes, and delicate broths that reflect the refined local cuisine. Return to Kyoto station for the Shinkansen back to the hotel, or stay overnight in Kyoto if budget allows.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing (~¥800–¥1,500 per person)
meals.lunch: Hanami picnic in Maruyama Park — purchase bento boxes, onigiri, and sakura mochi from nearby convenience stores or Nishiki Market (~¥1,000–¥1,800 per person)
meals.dinner: Mid-range Kyoto cuisine restaurant in Gion — tofu kaiseki set meal or obanzai (Kyoto-style small dishes) (~¥3,000–¥5,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cherry blossom timing in mid-April can vary year to year. Check the Japan Meteorological Corporation's sakura forecast closer to travel dates. Book Shinkansen tickets via the JR Pass or at the station — reserved seats are strongly recommended on weekends. Gion is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Kyoto. Begin the morning at Arashiyama — take a scenic train ride on the Sagano Romantic Train or local bus to this picturesque district. Walk through the iconic Arashiyama Bamboo Grove, where towering stalks of bamboo create an otherworldly green corridor. Arrive early (before 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds and experience the grove at its most peaceful and photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the bamboo grove, hike up to the Iwatayama Monkey Park — a 20-minute uphill trail leads to a hilltop sanctuary home to over 120 wild Japanese macaques (snow monkeys). Kids absolutely love feeding the monkeys through a wire mesh enclosure while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto below. Descend and explore Arashiyama's charming riverside shops and rent a rowboat on the Oi River for a relaxing family activity.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to central Kyoto and visit Nishiki Market — Kyoto's famous 'Kitchen Street' — for an early evening snack walk. Try grilled skewers, fresh tofu, pickled vegetables, and sweet mochi. Dinner at a casual noodle restaurant — Kyoto-style ramen or udon with a light dashi broth is a comforting family-friendly choice.

meals.breakfast: Local Kyoto café or hotel — Japanese morning set with rice, miso soup, and pickles (~¥800–¥1,500 per person)
meals.lunch: Arashiyama riverside café or bento from a local shop — try yudofu (hot tofu) or soba noodles (~¥1,200–¥2,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Kyoto ramen or udon restaurant near Nishiki Market (~¥1,000–¥1,800 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Iwatayama Monkey Park entrance fee is approximately ¥550 for adults and ¥250 for children. The uphill hike takes about 20 minutes and is moderately steep — wear comfortable shoes. Rowboat rentals on the Oi River cost approximately ¥1,500–¥2,000 for 30 minutes. Arrive at the bamboo grove before 9:00 AM for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Nara for a day trip — just 45 minutes from Kyoto by express train. Arrive at Nara Park, home to over 1,200 freely roaming sacred deer that bow for shika senbei (deer crackers) sold by park vendors. Children will be delighted feeding and interacting with the friendly deer. Walk through the park to Todai-ji Temple, home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue — a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Shrine, one of Japan's most important Shinto shrines, famous for its hundreds of bronze and stone lanterns lining the forested approach. Walk the scenic Naramachi district — a preserved merchant quarter with traditional townhouses converted into cafés, craft shops, and galleries. Pick up handmade Nara crafts as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto for dinner. Try a shabu-shabu or sukiyaki hot pot restaurant — a fun, interactive dining experience where the family cooks thinly sliced beef and vegetables in a communal pot at the table. This is a beloved Japanese family dining tradition and a great mid-range splurge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store before departing (~¥800–¥1,200 per person)
meals.lunch: Nara Park area café or restaurant — try kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi), a Nara specialty (~¥1,200–¥2,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Shabu-shabu or sukiyaki restaurant in Kyoto — all-you-can-eat options available at mid-range prices (~¥2,500–¥4,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Deer crackers (shika senbei) cost approximately ¥200 per bundle. Todai-ji entrance fee is ¥600 for adults and ¥300 for children. Nara is easily accessible from Kyoto via the Kintetsu Nara Line (approximately ¥700 one way). Keep bags held firmly — the deer are friendly but opportunistic and may nibble on bags or maps!

day_by_day.morning: Return to Tokyo or explore a new region. This day is dedicated to the Traditional Samurai and Ninja Experience — one of the most memorable activities for families in Japan. Dress in authentic samurai armor or ninja costumes and learn basic sword techniques, ninja star throwing (shuriken), and stealthy ninja movements from expert instructors. Many studios in Tokyo or Kyoto offer English-language sessions designed for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the samurai/ninja experience, visit a nearby traditional craft workshop. Try your hand at Japanese calligraphy (shodo), origami paper folding, or pottery making at a local cultural center. These hands-on workshops are widely available at mid-range prices and make for wonderful take-home memories and keepsakes.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the family's inner warriors with a hearty dinner at a teppanyaki restaurant — watch a skilled chef cook wagyu beef, seafood, and vegetables on an iron griddle right at your table with theatrical flair. A fun and delicious experience that kids and adults equally enjoy.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local bakery — Japanese melon pan or croissant with coffee/juice (~¥600–¥1,200 per person)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the samurai experience venue — Japanese curry rice (kare raisu), a beloved family-friendly staple (~¥800–¥1,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Teppanyaki restaurant — set course with soup, salad, protein, vegetables, rice, and dessert (~¥3,500–¥6,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Samurai and Ninja Experience in advance — popular studios include Samurai Kembu Theater (Kyoto) or Samurai & Ninja Museum (Tokyo). Sessions typically last 60–90 minutes and cost approximately ¥4,000–¥8,000 per person. Photos in costume are included. Calligraphy or origami workshops typically cost ¥1,500–¥3,000 per person for a 60-minute session.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate this day to Tokyo's family-friendly attractions. Start with a visit to Ueno Park and Zoo — Japan's oldest zoo, home to giant pandas, gorillas, and hundreds of other species. The park itself is a beautiful green oasis and may still have late cherry blossom trees in bloom. The Tokyo National Museum within Ueno Park offers fascinating exhibits on Japanese history, samurai artifacts, and ancient art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara — Tokyo's electric town — for an afternoon of anime, manga, gaming arcades, and electronics shopping. Visit a multi-story game center (Game Taito Station or Sega Akihabara) and try crane games, taiko drumming arcade games, and photo booth machines (purikura). Kids and teens will be in their element. Browse character merchandise shops for Pokémon, Studio Ghibli, and anime collectibles.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Akihabara or nearby Asakusa district. Visit Asakusa's Senso-ji Temple illuminated at night — one of Tokyo's most atmospheric evening sights. Browse Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional snacks and souvenirs before choosing a restaurant for dinner. Try tempura — a Tokyo specialty — at a mid-range tempura restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local kissaten (traditional Japanese café) — morning set with toast, egg, and coffee (~¥600–¥1,200 per person)
meals.lunch: Ueno Park area restaurant or bento — try yoshoku (Japanese-Western fusion) dishes like omurice or hamburger steak (~¥1,000–¥1,800 per person)
meals.dinner: Mid-range tempura restaurant in Asakusa — set meal with shrimp, vegetables, and rice (~¥2,000–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ueno Zoo admission is approximately ¥600 for adults and ¥200 for children. Tokyo National Museum admission is ¥1,000 for adults; children under 18 are free. Senso-ji Temple is free to enter and spectacular at night. Keep an eye on children in Akihabara's busy streets — it can get crowded on weekday afternoons.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Harajuku and Meiji Shrine for a beautiful morning combining nature and culture. Begin at Meiji Jingu Shrine, set within a tranquil 70-hectare forested sanctuary in the heart of Tokyo. Walk the grand gravel path lined with towering camphor trees to the main shrine, observe Shinto rituals, and write wishes on ema wooden plaques. A serene and deeply cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street in Harajuku — Tokyo's famous youth fashion and street food paradise. Try a rainbow cotton candy, crepe filled with strawberries and cream, or a Harajuku dog (corn dog with unique toppings). Browse quirky fashion boutiques and character shops. Then head to Omotesando — Harajuku's upscale tree-lined boulevard — for window shopping and café hopping.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shinjuku for the evening. Take a free elevator ride to the 45th-floor Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observation Deck for a stunning panoramic nighttime view of the Tokyo skyline — completely free of charge. Afterward, enjoy dinner in Shinjuku's vibrant restaurant district — try a yakiniku (Japanese BBQ) restaurant where the family grills their own marinated meats at the table.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café (~¥800–¥1,500 per person)
meals.lunch: Harajuku street food — crepes, takoyaki octopus balls, and Harajuku dogs (~¥800–¥1,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Yakiniku Japanese BBQ restaurant in Shinjuku — mid-range set with assorted meats, vegetables, and rice (~¥2,500–¥4,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is free to enter; the inner garden (Gyoen) charges a small fee of ¥500. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observation Deck is open until 22:30 (last entry 22:00) and is completely free — one of Tokyo's best free views. Shinjuku's restaurant district (Kabukicho and Memory Lane/Omoide Yokocho) is lively and best explored with older children.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Japan — make it special. Visit teamLab Planets in Toyosu (if not already visited teamLab Borderless) for a different immersive digital art experience, or revisit a favorite neighborhood. Alternatively, spend the morning at a local onsen (hot spring bath) if the hotel or a nearby facility offers one — a quintessential Japanese relaxation ritual to end the trip on a peaceful note.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Tokyo Station's underground shopping complex — one of the best places in Japan to buy omiyage (souvenir gifts) including regional sweets, matcha products, sake, and character goods. Pick up Tokyo Banana, Shiroi Koibito cookies, and specialty wagashi sweets for friends and family back home. Head back to the hotel to collect luggage and begin the journey to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart for Narita or Haneda Airport. Allow plenty of time — at least 3 hours before international departure. Enjoy a final Japanese meal at the airport — many terminals have excellent ramen, sushi, and tempura restaurants. Reflect on 10 incredible days of cherry blossoms, culture, family adventures, and unforgettable memories.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy a final Japanese morning meal (~¥800–¥1,500 per person)
meals.lunch: Tokyo Station food hall or nearby restaurant — try a final bowl of ramen or a katsu sandwich (katsu sando) (~¥1,000–¥2,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant — quality ramen, sushi, or tempura at Narita or Haneda Airport (~¥1,500–¥3,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Return your Suica/Pasmo IC cards at the airport for a refund of remaining balance (minus a ¥220 handling fee). Declare any purchases over your home country's customs allowance. Japan's airport duty-free shopping is excellent — check for last-minute cosmetics, whisky, and electronics deals. Arrive at the airport with at least 3 hours to spare for international flights.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Join locals for picnics beneath thousands of blooming sakura trees, enjoy street food stalls selling yakitori and dango, and soak in the festive atmosphere. Perfect for families with open spaces for children to play.

experiences.name: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a breathtaking world of interactive digital art installations where light, sound, and color blend seamlessly. Children and adults alike will be mesmerized by the borderless rooms that react to movement. A truly unique cultural and artistic experience that blends technology with Japanese aesthetics.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Japan's most iconic food market with a guided family-friendly walking tour. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette), matcha sweets, and grilled seafood skewers. Learn about Japanese culinary traditions and the importance of fresh ingredients in Japanese cuisine. Kids will love the variety of street snacks.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo forest of Arashiyama, then hike up to the Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Families can feed the monkeys from inside a viewing hut while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a rickshaw ride through the scenic area for extra fun.

experiences.name: Traditional Samurai and Ninja Experience
experiences.description: Dress your family in authentic samurai armor or ninja costumes and learn basic sword techniques and ninja skills from trained instructors. This hands-on cultural workshop gives children and adults a thrilling glimpse into Japan's feudal history. Includes a photo session in full costume and a certificate of completion for the kids.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Rest — Flight UA lands at 22:30. No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival & Rest — No afternoon activities scheduled prior to landing.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival at 22:30. Private luxury transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a welcome amenity prepared by the resort (sake, seasonal wagashi sweets). Light room service available.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: In-flight or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — request a curated bento or ramen bowl to ease into Japanese cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport meet-and-greet service and private car transfer for a seamless arrival. Request early check-in amenities and a pillow menu for jet-lag recovery. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort breakfast followed by a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront. Acclimate to the time zone with a spa session at the resort's premium wellness center — book a traditional Japanese onsen soak or shiatsu massage to reset after the long flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate resort surroundings. Visit a nearby local shrine or coastal promenade for a first taste of Japanese culture and architecture. Pick up a few artisan souvenirs at a curated local boutique near the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant. Opt for an omakase kaiseki menu — a multi-course Japanese haute cuisine experience featuring seasonal spring ingredients and local seafood.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — fresh fruit, Japanese tamago, miso soup, and pastries
meals.lunch: Light poolside or beachfront lunch at the resort — grilled fish, edamame, and cold soba
meals.dinner: Omakase kaiseki dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's fine-dining restaurant — pair with premium sake or a curated Japanese whisky flight

day_by_day.notes: Use Day 2 as a soft landing day. Avoid heavy sightseeing to fully recover from jet lag. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings and private transfers with the resort concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Depart by private luxury vehicle to Kyoto (travel time varies by resort location — allow 2–3 hours if traveling from coastal area). Upon arrival, head directly to Maruyama Park for the Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience. Admire Kyoto's iconic weeping cherry tree in full spring bloom, stroll the park's landscaped paths, and enjoy a private guided hanami picnic arranged under the blossoms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park. Walk through the towering emerald bamboo corridor, then hike up Iwatayama to the Monkey Park where Japanese macaques roam freely with panoramic views of Kyoto below. A private guide enhances the experience with cultural storytelling.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Kyoto's Gion district — Japan's most celebrated geisha quarter. Dine at a premier kaiseki restaurant in a traditional machiya townhouse. Optional: arrange a private maiko (apprentice geisha) cultural performance during dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — Japanese-style with rice, grilled fish, and pickles
meals.lunch: Private hanami picnic in Maruyama Park — curated bento boxes with premium sushi, seasonal tempura, and matcha from a top Kyoto caterer
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner in Gion — Michelin-starred or highly acclaimed restaurant such as a traditional Kyoto ryotei; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Mid-April is peak cherry blossom season — Maruyama Park will be busy. A private guide and early arrival (by 9:00 AM) ensures the best experience before crowds peak. Confirm Monkey Park is family-friendly for all ages in your group.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Samurai and Ninja Experience in Kyoto. Dress the entire family in authentic samurai armor or ninja costumes, learn basic sword techniques, shuriken throwing, and ninja stealth moves from a professional instructor. This immersive cultural activity is a highlight for families and unforgettable for children and adults alike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nijo Castle and its famous 'nightingale floors,' then explore the Kyoto Imperial Palace grounds. A private cultural guide provides deep historical context about the shogunate era, tying perfectly into the morning's samurai theme.
day_by_day.evening: Scenic return journey toward Tokyo or onward destination. If staying in Kyoto overnight, enjoy a relaxed dinner at a premium teppanyaki restaurant where a skilled chef performs tableside.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Kyoto if staying overnight, or resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a renowned Kyoto tofu cuisine restaurant (yudofu) near Nijo Castle — a uniquely Kyoto culinary tradition
meals.dinner: Premium teppanyaki dinner — Wagyu beef, seasonal vegetables, and fresh seafood prepared tableside

day_by_day.notes: Book the Samurai and Ninja Experience well in advance as family slots fill up quickly during cherry blossom season. Confirm whether armor fitting is available for children. Photography is usually included — request a dedicated photographer for premium packages.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Tokyo via the Shinkansen (bullet train) — book a private Green Car (first-class) compartment for the family. The journey from Kyoto to Tokyo takes approximately 2 hours 15 minutes and is itself a premium experience with Mt. Fuji views on clear days. Arrive at Tokyo Station and transfer to a luxury city hotel or return to resort if Tokyo-based.
day_by_day.afternoon: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum experience. Immerse the entire family in Tokyo's world-famous interactive digital art installations — boundless rooms of flowing light, sound, and motion that respond to touch. A truly awe-inspiring, multi-sensory experience perfect for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale Odaiba waterfront district. Enjoy panoramic views of Tokyo Bay and the Rainbow Bridge illuminated at night. Dinner at a premium restaurant with a private bay view.

meals.breakfast: Bento breakfast box from a premium Kyoto station vendor (Isetan or similar) enjoyed on the Shinkansen
meals.lunch: Lunch near Teamlab Borderless — try a high-end ramen or sushi restaurant in the Odaiba or Ariake area
meals.dinner: Waterfront fine dining in Odaiba — contemporary Japanese cuisine with Tokyo Bay views; consider a restaurant with private dining room for the family

day_by_day.notes: Teamlab Borderless tickets must be purchased well in advance online — the museum frequently sells out weeks ahead, especially during peak spring season. Wear comfortable shoes as you will walk extensively through the installations.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour. Join a premium guided family-friendly walking tour of Japan's most iconic food market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelet), grilled scallops, matcha soft-serve, and seasonal street foods. A private guide curates the best stalls and explains the cultural significance of each ingredient.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the historic Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest and most beloved Buddhist temple. Walk the Nakamise shopping street for premium souvenir shopping: lacquerware, hand-painted fans, silk items, and artisan crafts. Optional: rickshaw ride through the traditional Asakusa district.
day_by_day.evening: Ascend the Tokyo Skytree (world's second tallest tower) for a breathtaking panoramic sunset view over the city. Reserve a table at the tower's premium restaurant for dinner with a 360-degree Tokyo skyline view.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel before the early market tour
meals.lunch: The Tsukiji Food Tour IS the lunch experience — a progressive tasting of 8–12 premium market bites including otoro (fatty tuna) sushi
meals.dinner: Tokyo Skytree premium restaurant — contemporary French-Japanese fusion cuisine with floor-to-ceiling city views

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji Outer Market tour should start early (around 8:00–9:00 AM) for the freshest products and smaller crowds. The inner wholesale market is closed to tourists, but the outer market remains a world-class culinary destination. Book a private guide for a more personalized and educational experience.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the upscale Harajuku and Omotesando neighborhoods. Visit the iconic Meiji Shrine set within a serene forested sanctuary — a peaceful contrast to the city buzz. A private Shinto cultural guide explains rituals, fortune slips (omikuji), and the significance of torii gates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury shopping along Omotesando Avenue — Tokyo's answer to the Champs-Élysées. Browse flagship stores of Japanese designers (Issey Miyake, Comme des Garçons) and international luxury brands. Visit the Omotesando Hills complex for curated boutiques and artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Shinjuku's premium dining district. Visit the famous Memory Lane (Omoide Yokocho) for atmospheric photos, then dine at a top-tier Shinjuku restaurant — consider a private room at a premium yakitori or shabu-shabu establishment.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Japanese-style spread with miso, rice, grilled fish, and seasonal pickles
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium café or restaurant in Omotesando Hills — try a refined Japanese pasta or seasonal bento
meals.dinner: Premium shabu-shabu dinner in Shinjuku — A5 Wagyu beef cooked tableside in a dashi broth; private room recommended for families

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is most atmospheric in the early morning — aim to arrive by 9:00 AM. The forested approach path (1 km of towering torii gates) is especially beautiful in spring light. Omotesando shopping is best in the afternoon when stores are fully staffed.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (approximately 2 hours from Tokyo by Shinkansen/limited express). Explore the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — an extraordinarily ornate mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu surrounded by ancient cedar forests. A private guide brings the samurai-era history to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Nikko's Kanman-ga-fuchi Abyss — a serene riverside walk lined with mossy stone Jizo statues beneath towering cedar trees. Visit Rinno-ji Temple and its stunning Sanbutsudo (Three Buddha Hall). In spring, the surrounding mountains may still have cherry blossoms at higher elevations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by private or first-class train. Relaxed evening at leisure — optional dinner at the hotel's restaurant or a neighborhood sushi counter for an intimate omakase experience.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure to Nikko
meals.lunch: Traditional yuba (tofu skin) cuisine lunch in Nikko — a local specialty unique to the region, served at a refined traditional restaurant
meals.dinner: Intimate omakase sushi counter in Tokyo — 10–15 course chef's selection with premium nigiri; book a counter with only 8–10 seats for an exclusive experience

day_by_day.notes: Nikko is a full-day excursion — depart by 8:00 AM to maximize time at the shrines. The Tosho-gu complex involves significant walking and some steep stone staircases — comfortable walking shoes are essential. Private guide highly recommended to unlock the rich history of the site.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Yanaka district — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old-town (shitamachi) neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Wander narrow lanes lined with traditional wooden houses, independent craft shops, and local temples. A private cultural walking tour reveals Tokyo's authentic pre-modern character.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit teamLab Planets in Toyosu (different from Borderless — equally spectacular). Walk through immersive water and flower rooms where digital art merges with physical sensation. Ideal for families seeking another world-class interactive art experience. Follow with a visit to the Toyosu Market observation deck for views of Japan's premier seafood wholesale market.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-to-Tokyo dinner at one of the city's celebrated Michelin-starred restaurants. Consider a French-Japanese fusion experience at a three-Michelin-star venue, or a premier teppanyaki restaurant with A5 Wagyu as the centerpiece.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy a final leisurely morning meal
meals.lunch: Lunch in Yanaka at a charming local café or traditional Japanese sweet shop (wagashi) — try anmitsu or warabi mochi
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred farewell dinner — reserve 2–3 months in advance; dress code applies at most venues

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets also requires advance ticket booking. It is a different and equally powerful experience from Borderless — both are worth visiting on the same trip. The Yanaka cemetery is also beautiful in spring with cherry blossoms lining its main avenue.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure. Last-minute luxury shopping at Ginza — Tokyo's most prestigious shopping district. Visit the Itoya flagship stationery store for premium Japanese paper goods and gifts. Browse Mitsukoshi or Matsuya department stores for curated Japanese crafts, food gifts, and fashion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort for a final afternoon of relaxation. Enjoy the beachfront, resort pool, or a final spa treatment. Reflect on the journey over afternoon tea with matcha and seasonal wagashi sweets served by the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner at the resort — request a private beachfront dining setup if available. A curated menu celebrating the best of Japan: premium sashimi, grilled Wagyu, seasonal vegetables, and a toast with premium Japanese champagne or Nikka whisky.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or resort breakfast — savor the final Japanese morning meal
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Ginza — try a refined tonkatsu (premium breaded pork cutlet) restaurant or a high-end soba establishment
meals.dinner: Private beachfront farewell dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — personalized menu curated with the resort chef; pair with a premium sake or Japanese whisky selection

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure logistics today — arrange airport transfer, reconfirm flight details, and complete any duty-free purchases. Many premium Japanese food items (wagyu, matcha, sake) make excellent gifts and can be vacuum-sealed or packed for travel. Allow extra time at the airport for Japan's thorough security and customs procedures.
